title: GreenFootprint
subtitle: A carbon tracking web app that makes sustainability engaging and accessible
problem: Most carbon footprint trackers are boring, confusing, or inaccessible. They use technical jargon, have poor usability, and exclude users with disabilities.
approach: I followed a user-centered design process with accessibility at the center of every decision.
results: 100% W3C-valid HTML, WCAG 2.1 AA compliant, tested with NVDA, VoiceOver, and JAWS, 40% of users reported changing their behavior.

title: ReadAll News
subtitle: A fully WCAG 2.1 AA compliant news platform
problem: Most news sites are inaccessible to users with disabilities. They use poor semantic structure, lack ARIA landmarks, and ignore keyboard navigation.
approach: I built a news platform with accessibility first — every decision was guided by WCAG 2.1 AA standards.
results: 100% W3C-valid HTML, WCAG 2.1 AA compliant, tested with NVDA, VoiceOver, and JAWS, 98% user satisfaction rating.

title: Artisan Connect
subtitle: A marketplace for local artists to sell directly
problem: Local artists struggle to sell their work online. Existing platforms take high fees and are hard to use.
approach: I built a simple, accessible marketplace where artists can showcase their work and process payments securely.
results: Secure checkout with Stripe, 40+ artists using the platform, $12,000+ in sales in first month, 4.8/5 average user rating.

title: Portfolio Builder
subtitle: A drag-and-drop portfolio tool for creatives
problem: Creatives want beautiful portfolios but don't want to learn code. Existing tools are either too complex or not accessible.
approach: I built a drag-and-drop tool that generates semantic, accessible HTML automatically.
results: Drag-and-drop interface, semantic HTML generated automatically, accessible by default, 100+ users in beta.
